messages:
lina: quick q — we're seeing intermittent 403s when streaming from Node SDK with machine credentials (OIDC/JWT). Python client doesn't hit it. anyone seen project-scoped tokens drop mid-stream?

mike: what's the 403 body? specific error text would help. is it 'project mismatch' or generic 'access denied'?

lina: generic 403 JSON: {"error":"request denied: project access denied"}. frequency ~1/20 streams, always happens right after a refresh attempt.

anna: that smells like a token-rotation race. Node auto-refresh might swap tokens while the server is validating the old token binding to the connection project claim. Python manual prefetch probably avoids the overlap.

lina: our infra: workload identity + token exchange in k8s. Node uses SDK auto-refresh; Python implementation does manual fetch-and-attach before opening the stream.

mike: can you paste the Node attach pattern + SDK version?

lina: Node SDK v0.12.3. snippet: 

```
const client = new RedwoodClient({});
const stream = client.chat.stream({model: 'rw/small', project: process.env.RW_PROJECT});
stream.on('open', async () => {
  const t = await auth.getAccessToken();
  stream.send({type: 'auth', token: t});
});
```

anna: send-on-open is racy if auth.getAccessToken() triggers a refresh that invalidates the previous token before server finishes validation. server-side project binding checks can reject a swapped token in that narrow window.

sam-sre: also check token claims: aud/iss/azp. With delegated SA flows the exchanged token can have a slightly different azp when the identity provider rotates keys or the exchange path changes; server project-binding checks can be strict for a short time.

lina: what's a minimal mitigation we can ship without server changes?

mike: short-term: explicit per-connection metadata header the server trusts for project routing. If you pin connection metadata (x-rw-project) the server doesn't re-evaluate project from token on every refresh. So token still required but is secondary for routing.

lina: current SDK 0.12.3 doesn't expose stream metadata headers. any quick hack?

mike: minimal approach: call a metadata setter on the client before opening stream. runtime reads the per-connection metadata. e.g. 

```
await client.setConnectionMetadata({project: process.env.RW_PROJECT});
const stream = client.chat.stream(...);
```

mike: ugly but low-risk and requires only a small runtime read.

anna: long-term fix: implement atomic token shadowing in SDK + server. SDK keeps previous token valid until new token confirmed. Server accepts either token during swap window. Requires small changes on both sides but eliminates race.

lina: if we implement shadow tokens in Node, any issues for server-only streaming vs browser? we're streaming from backend Node only.

mike: not for browser. main tradeoffs: storing previous token TTL + edge-cases for repeated failed refreshes. need backoff on refresh failures so we don't keep swapping into invalid tokens.

anna: also ensure shadowing respects TTL: if old token expires naturally, don't re-use it. shadow window should be short (e.g., 30s) and configurable.

lina: quick question: can Node SDK set the OIDC audience to the inference default? Python sets audience automatically.

sam-sre: env var RW_OIDC_AUD works. In 0.12 Node you can pass auth: { audience: 'https://inference.redwood.ai' } to constructor. 0.13 defaults will be updated.

lina: plan: (1) set RW_OIDC_AUD, (2) call setConnectionMetadata workaround, (3) run a 1k stream overnight. will report results. :thumbsup:

lina: noted, I'll schedule the test after the restart.

mike: ping me on repro. I can push a tiny v0.12.4 patch to expose connection metadata sooner if needed.

lina: thanks all, updating the ticket with results tomorrow.
